solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Silent leaving clubs? Only a bit in Glasgow

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so the abbreviation that follows drops out of the word

blocks.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer's question about quietly leaving the clubs behind, followed by a remark about Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: TACIT loses its C to leave TAIT; 'in Glasgow' marks it as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: TAIT is a Scots word for a small quantity, so it is a dialect equivalent of a little bit.

clue.text: Sound quality not so fierce around bass

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other

blocks.note: first part of TAMER, less fierce
B is the abbreviation for bass

explanation.surface: A sound engineer softens the bass to improve the tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamber is an old spelling of timbre, the distinctive quality or colour of a sound.

clue.text: Materially wrong about potassium measurement in labs

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged
about means round, so the rearranged letters go round the element

blocks.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A lab technician's potassium reading turns out to be substantially wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkalimetry is the chemical measurement of the strength or amount of alkali in a sample.

clue.text: Briefs a nipper lifted up

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a gnat bites, so it nips

explanation.surface: Underwear bitten by a small child and then pulled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' suggests a child, but here it is a biting insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a skimpy pair of briefs, a kind of string bikini bottom.

clue.text: Love kiss on the kisser from an African bird

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
kisser is slang for the mouth, and so is pecker in Chambers

explanation.surface: A romantic picture of a loving kiss planted on someone's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kisser' here is slang for the mouth, and PECKER is another slang word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxpecker is an African starling that rides on cattle and game, eating ticks off their hides.

clue.text: Sort of ranks remaining

blocks.note: first meaning: ... ranks are soldiers below commissioned officers

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a fill-in-the-blank: the military phrase for enlisted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Other completes the army phrase for non-officers and also means the ones left over.

clue.text: Cordial company sharing a seat

indicators.note: sharing a space means sitting inside it alongside others

blocks.note: per means a, as in once a day
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Friendly people squeezing up together on one bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective for friendly company, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Persicot is a liqueur flavoured with peach or apricot kernels, so it is a cordial.

clue.text: Old head of English in school uttered the call

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word for the school
'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'English'

blocks.note: start of COED, a coeducational school
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A former head of the English department shouting across a schoolyard.
explanation.walkthrough: COOEE is the Australian bush call used to attract attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooeed is the past tense of cooee, so it means gave that long shrill call.

clue.text: County resident not right to reveal pig iron on board

indicators.note: not with a letter's word means that letter is taken away

blocks.note: ledger in Chambers can mean resident, as a ledger ambassador
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Kent local reveals the iron ballast aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentledge is pig iron laid in a ship's hold as permanent ballast.

clue.text: Given a new role take advanced supersonic transport

blocks.note: REC abbreviates recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
the initials of the advanced supersonic transport project

explanation.surface: An actor recast to fly on Concorde's successor.
explanation.walkthrough: The R on prescriptions stands for recipe, take.
explanation.definitionFit: To recast an actor is to give them a different part, assigning a new role.

clue.text: Stella drunk in Rock could get you this

definitions.text: Stella drunk in Rock could get you this

indicators.note: a drunk person's words come out jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
in says one set of letters sits inside another

blocks.note: first half of AA, a rough lava rock
the six letters of Stella rearranged
second half of AA, the lava

explanation.surface: Getting drunk on Stella Artois lager on the rocks would leave anyone confused.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is a Hawaiian word for rough, clinkery lava, used often in crosswords. The whole clue also says that too much Stella leaves you befuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all at sea is to be bewildered, which is how a heavy drinker of lager might feel.

clue.text: Shy about going before audience in dressing room

indicators.note: going means departing, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: the house is a theatre audience

explanation.surface: A shy performer hides in the dressing room before facing the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' removes RE from the front of RETIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiring house was the dressing room behind the stage of an Elizabethan theatre, where actors attired themselves.

clue.text: Short of backing many in choir impromptu getting out of tune

indicators.note: falling short of a word means its last letter is missing
backing means going in the reverse direction, so the shortened word is read from the end
something impromptu is improvised on the spot, so these letters get a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: many cut short and turned round

explanation.surface: Many members of a choir singing without rehearsal are drifting off pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' takes the Y off many; the remaining letters are turned round and then mixed with in and choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Inharmonic means lacking harmony, so a note that is inharmonic is discordant or off pitch.

clue.text: Lightermen last to encourage shelducks

indicators.note: last to a word points at its final letter only

blocks.note: lightermen work flat-bottomed boats, so they are bargees

explanation.surface: Boatmen on the river urging on a flock of ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargoose is a Chambers name for the shelduck, and its plural is the word in the grid.

clue.text: What some TT reformers might do for an explanation

blocks.clueFragment: What some TT reformers might do
What some TT reformers might do

explanation.surface: Teetotal campaigners wanting to justify their reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal; such reformers would ration ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind something, so it is an explanation.

clue.text: Wrought iron case in outline

indicators.note: wrought means worked into shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A wrought-iron box sketched in outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline of a plot, or a sketch of how events may unfold.

clue.text: Fruit from the east without flavour mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
in an across answer, reading from the east means right to left

blocks.note: silent, as in silent spirit, is neutral and unflavoured; mostly drops the T

explanation.surface: An exotic fruit from the Orient that turns out to be rather bland.
explanation.walkthrough: Silent spirit is distilling jargon for spirit with no flavour; trim it and read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: NELIS is a variety of winter pear, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Recall movement in scores of MacMillan

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Remembering a movement from one of James MacMillan's musical scores.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface misleads: scores are scratches, and MacMillan, a Scottish name, signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a rit is a scratch or cut, so rits are scratches, the other sense of scores.

clue.text: Stress about infectious diseases? It happens

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: accent is stress on a syllable
ID is the abbreviation for infectious diseases

explanation.surface: Anxiety over catching infections in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'accidents happen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unplanned event, something that simply happens without intention.

clue.text: A little boy catches fly

indicators.note: whatever catches something holds it inside

blocks.note: first letter of SON, a boy
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: A small boy snatching a fly out of the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Smidgeon is a variant spelling of smidgen, a tiny amount, so a little.

clue.text: Payment one accepted for concave moulding

blocks.note: scot is an old tax or payment, as in scot-free
A is the abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: A craftsman's invoice being accepted for some decorative plasterwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A scotia is a hollow concave moulding, especially at the base of a column.

clue.text: Cobblers urge beginning with last

indicators.note: beginning points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Shoemakers urged to start with the last, the foot-shaped block they work on.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers is British slang for nonsense, and a last is the cobbler's foot-shaped form.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is foolish talk, just what cobblers means in British slang.

clue.text: Tense journalist fellow union's leader ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so that letter is removed
'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'union'

explanation.surface: A reporter feels nervous when the union boss refuses to speak to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy and tense both describe someone nervous and on edge.

clue.text: Endless corruption absorbed by the old American

indicators.note: endless means both ends are cut off the word
what is absorbed by something goes inside it

blocks.note: first letter of YE, old form of the

explanation.surface: Endless corruption soaked up by an old American.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name for a US citizen.

clue.text: Freeman, company boss attached to both sides

explanation.surface: A free man who is also a company chief, siding with everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceorl was an Anglo-Saxon freeman of the lowest rank, a churl.

clue.text: The old take plan without a pinch of salt

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: Following a plan or recipe while skipping the pinch of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Deign in an obsolete sense meant to accept or take something, as well as condescend.

clue.text: Students below, look up in group of trees

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading from bottom to top
below in a down answer puts this part underneath the next one

blocks.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Students lying under a tree and looking up into the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Alnus is the botanical genus of the alders, a group of related trees.

clue.text: Inconsistent person turned up before Christmas over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the festival word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A fickle guest appeared just before the Christmas holiday ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like a reversal signal but simply means arrived; 'over' does the reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameleon is an old spelling of chameleon, used figuratively of a changeable person.

clue.text: Go around a green for limestone deposit

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: start of TRINE, an archaic slang word for go

explanation.surface: A golfer walking round the putting surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests golf, but it is the heraldic colour. TRINE is an old cant word meaning to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Travertine is a pale calcareous rock deposited by mineral springs, a form of limestone.

clue.text: Insult chaps spoken of in front

indicators.note: spoken of means said out loud, so the word is chosen by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone insults a group of men who are being talked about to their faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A front is a false outward show, and a disguise is likewise an appearance hiding the truth.

clue.text: Nut eating honey and cereal

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside

blocks.note: first letter of ACORN, the nut
mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy

explanation.surface: A breakfast picture of nuts, honey and cereal together.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelcorn is emmer, a kind of wheat grown as grain, so it is a cereal.

clue.text: Unfinished search for item in playground up north

indicators.note: unfinished means the end is missing, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a sweep is a thorough search

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a hunt for a lost toy in a playground in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Swee is Scots for a swing, a standard piece of playground equipment.
